g4ela-23-1-morphology: Two new roots. Lev means lift. Think of an elevator lifting you up. Sist means stand. When you resist, you stand against something. Every word today is lifting or standing. Ask which one, then sew the patch.
g4ela-23-2-grammar: Faster can describe a horse, or it can describe how the horse runs. When it describes a thing, it’s an adjective. When it tells how someone did something, it’s an adverb. So don’t just spot the comparing words. Ask what each one is describing.
g4ela-23-3-spelling: Here’s the trick for lazy vowels. In abolition, you can barely hear the o. So find a relative of the word where that part gets the stress. Abolish. Now the o is loud and clear. Say the relative, and the spelling shows itself.
g4ela-23-4-grammar: Editing day. Some comparing words are already right, so leave them alone. Look for two mistakes. One is doubling up, like more louder. The other is an adjective doing an adverb’s job, like moved quicker. Fix those, then read the sentence out loud to check.
